{{Quote|A meteor shower. The season of the skyfall has come again.|The [[The Dark Woman|Dark Woman]] witnessing a meteor shower on a jungle world|<ref name="SW 30">[[Star Wars (1998) 30|''Star Wars'' (1998) 30]]</ref>}}
[[File:Skyfall.png|thumb|right|260px|A meteor shower on a jungle world in the [[Kamdon system/Legends|Kamdon system]]]]
'''Meteor showers'''<ref name="Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> or '''meteor storms'''<ref name="Escape Into Terror">{{DroidsCite|Escape Into Terror}}</ref> were common celestial events in which [[Realspace/Legends|space]]-born rocks in the form of [[Meteor/Legends|meteors]] entered a [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]].<ref name="SW 30" /> The falling rocks usually burned up or exploded as they entered the atmosphere, but some might make it to the ground or collide with a [[Starship/Legends|ship]] in flight, which could cause significant destruction. Meteor showers in the upper atmosphere of a planet could be especially dangerous for passing ships, as most of the space rocks had not yet been burned away.<ref name="The Unknown Regions">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:Meteor_strike.png|thumb|left|250px|Meteorites from a shower strike the surface of Rishi moon.]]
The jungle [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Borleias/Legends|Borleias]] was known to undergo particularly violent [[Meteor/Legends|meteor]] showers. [[Tasar system|Tasari]] legend told of a monumental meteor shower that created the [[Deadbelt]].<ref name="Star Wars Adventure Journal 15">[[Star Wars Adventure Journal 15|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 15]]</ref>

A [[Unidentified jungle world (Kamdon system)|jungle world]] in the [[Kamdon system/Legends|Kamdon system]] experienced seasonal meteor showers where meteors would enter the planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and tear through its surface, destroying untold acres of foliage, but also brought nutrients that the jungle needed to grow.<ref name="SW 30" />

While stationed on the remote [[Rishi moon]] [[Listening post/Legends|listening post]], the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] detected an incoming meteor shower and raised the defensive shields. Hidden among the interstellar debris were multiple [[Droch-class boarding ship/Legends|pod hunters]] occupied by [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commandos]].<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Roark Garnet/Legends|Roark Garnet's]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]], ''[[Dorion Discus]]'', suffered damage in a meteor storm. The ship's [[fusion generator]]s were damaged, and Garnet was lucky the [[magnetic bottle]] did not fail.<ref name="RPG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>

A common espionage tactic involved concealing [[Starship/Legends|starships]] within a mass of meteors. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the crew of ''[[Mon Remonda/Legends|Mon Remonda]]'' diverted a series of [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] to create a meteor shower over [[Saffalore]] which provided cover for [[Wraith Squadron]]'s subsequent [[Mission to Saffalore|raid]].<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Since the [[Realspace/Legends|space]] rocks that enter the [[Unidentified jungle world (Kamdon system)|jungle world's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] in [[Star Wars (1998) 30|''Star Wars'' (1998) 30]] hit the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] surface,<ref name="SW 30" /> it is technically a ''[[Meteorite storm|meteorite shower]]'' rather than a meteor shower:<ref name="Britannica">{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/science/meteor|text=meteorite shower|quote='''meteorite shower''', swarm of separate but related meteorites that land on Earth's surface at about the same time and place.|work=''[[Wikipedia:Encyclopedia Britannica|Encyclopedia Britannica]]''|archivedate=20230220121533}}</ref> A meteor is a ''[[Meteoroid/Legends|meteoroid]]'' (lumps of rock or [[Iron/Legends|iron]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] the sun)<ref name="National Georgraphic">{{WebCite|url=https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/meteoroid|text=Meteoroid|quote=Meteoroids are lumps of rock or iron that orbit the sun, just as planets, asteroids, and comets do. (...) Most meteoroids are created from asteroid impacts. As asteroids crash and break up, their debris is classified as meteoroids.|work=[[Wikipedia:National Geographic|National Geographic]]|archivedate=20230519051742}}</ref> that enters Earth's, or another [[Planet/Legends|planet's]], [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] but burns up before it reaches the ground, which is why they're also called "shooting [[Star/Legends|stars]]." A ''[[Meteorite/Legends|meteorite]]'', on the other hand, is a meteoroid that enters Earths atmosphere and hits the ground.<ref name="NASA">{{WebCite|url=https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/asteroids-comets-and-meteors/meteors-and-meteorites|text=What's the difference between a meteor, meteoroid, and meteorite?|quote='''Meteoroids''' are objects in space that range in size from dust grains to small asteroids. Think of them as "space rocks." When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere (or that of another planet, like Mars) at high speed and burn up, the fireballs or "shooting stars" are called '''meteors'''. When a meteoroid survives a trip through the atmosphere and hits the ground, it's called a '''meteorite'''.|work=[[Wikipedia:NASA|NASA]]|archivedate=20230423090620}}</ref>
